Above 10 bar the gE rule (MHV1) would suit, but it has no set here. PR at 1698 kPa, a light gas with a polar liquid (Carbon dioxide + Methanol, Carbon dioxide + Water, Hydrogen + Methanol, Hydrogen + Water, Carbon monoxide + Methanol, Carbon monoxide + Water, Nitrogen + Methanol, Nitrogen + Water): above about 10 bar the method guide recommends a cubic equation with a gE mixing rule (rule 4 of docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md). CHEPTA's rule of that kind would be refused: PR + gE (MHV1): Methanol + Nitrogen, a light gas with a polar liquid, has no NRTL parameters fitted inside the rule (src/data/mhv1.json) and none in the databank, so its solubility would rest on no data (proposal 0018). Pairs fitted so far: carbon-dioxide + methanol, hydrogen + methanol, carbon-monoxide + methanol, methane + methanol, carbon-dioxide + water, hydrogen + water, carbon-monoxide + water, methane + water. Give the pair's NRTL parameters in mixing.nrtl, or use PR with its k_ij. So PR with its k_ij stays the one that runs; the rule needs an NRTL set for each such pair (docs/DATA_WANTED.md).

PR is the method here: Carbon dioxide, Hydrogen, Carbon monoxide, Nitrogen are light gases, which only an equation of state describes (gas-phase reactors and high-pressure loops are simulated so). For a liquid of the polar components alone (Methanol, Water) below about 10 bar, such as their distillation, an activity model (NRTL or UNIQUAC) would be more accurate (docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md).
